units.product: One independently identifiable product, open-source project, or independently surfaced design workspace represented by one canonical project directory.
units.teamLineage: The independently attributable product or maintainer lineage responsible for that record. Acquired and historical lineages remain distinct.
units.publicTeamBoundary: Public evidence usually cannot reveal stable internal squads. Team-like scope is therefore reported using both consolidated organization or maintainer umbrellas and distinct product or maintainer lineages, never as a precise headcount of internal teams.
units.organization: The canonical owning organization or maintainer umbrella used by this census to consolidate related team lineages. It is a research counting unit, not necessarily the ultimate legal corporate parent.
units.designDefinition: An operational answer to what the user is doing when the product calls or treats work as design. Definitions are multi-label because one product may embody several answers.
units.productForm: The primary user-facing packaging of the product in this snapshot. Each record receives exactly one primary form so the distribution is countable.
units.architectureFamily: A decisive implementation arrangement connecting artifact authority, visual projection, agent control, mutation, and persistence. Records have one primary family and may have additional families.

includeWhen: The object is an independently identifiable product, open-source project, or independently surfaced Design workspace rather than only a feature alias.
At least one evidenced ordinary-user loop treats visual or interactive creation, authoring, correction, decision, governance, translation, delivery, or coordination as Design work.
Public evidence establishes the product boundary and working artifact authority; historical entries also require an independently material lineage and explicit cutoff.
excludeWhen: It is only a generic model, API, or media generator without a design-specific artifact loop.
It is a generic coding or execution agent with no evidenced visual or Design-specific surface.
It is a traditional tool whose AI-native product or workspace cannot be independently evidenced.
It is an alias, rebrand, product mode, or surface already owned by a canonical record.
knownCoverageLimits: Discovery currently depends mainly on publicly reachable English- and Chinese-language primary material, public source and package registries, shipped distributions, and observable product surfaces.
Stealth teams, private deployments, inaccessible paid surfaces, and products documented only in unreviewed languages can be missed.
Closed products may contain distinct internal mechanisms that cannot be separated beyond their observable authority and protocol boundaries.

designDefinitions.title: Design as delegated creation
designDefinitions.operationalTest: A person supplies intent or references and an AI or agent creates and repeatedly refines the visual or interactive artifact.
designDefinitions.boundary: A one-shot template recommendation without an artifact refinement loop is insufficient.

designDefinitions.title: Design as native artifact authoring
designDefinitions.operationalTest: The central work is creating or editing a structured design, scene, page, site, or timeline graph that remains a first-class artifact.
designDefinitions.boundary: A screenshot or transient runtime DOM is not a native authoring artifact.

designDefinitions.title: Design as visual authoring of executable source
designDefinitions.operationalTest: A visual surface renders executable source or a running application and changes ultimately return to the code or workspace that owns implementation authority.
designDefinitions.boundary: One-way design export to code belongs to design-code translation unless later visual work returns to the same source authority.

designDefinitions.title: Design as runtime correction
designDefinitions.operationalTest: A person selects, annotates, adjusts, or demonstrates a change on a running artifact so an agent or deterministic writer can repair the implementation.
designDefinitions.boundary: Passive preview or screenshots without a targetable correction path are visual coordination instead.

designDefinitions.title: Design as variant exploration and decision
designDefinitions.operationalTest: The product makes alternative directions coexist, supports comparison or refinement, and has an explicit promotion or selection step.
designDefinitions.boundary: Undo history or sequential regeneration alone is not parallel design exploration.

designDefinitions.title: Design as system governance
designDefinitions.operationalTest: The product extracts, defines, publishes, applies, or validates reusable components, tokens, brand rules, or layout conventions that constrain later work.
designDefinitions.boundary: Merely accepting a color reference or component screenshot is not a governed design system.

designDefinitions.title: Design as design-code translation and grounding
designDefinitions.operationalTest: The decisive workflow converts, joins, or grounds identities, components, tokens, or structure across a design artifact and a codebase.
designDefinitions.boundary: Generic image-to-code reconstruction without preserved structure or repository grounding is delegated creation.

designDefinitions.title: Design as end-to-end product delivery
designDefinitions.operationalTest: Design work is inseparable from creating a functional app or site and advancing it through behavior, data, testing, publication, or deployment.
designDefinitions.boundary: A runnable prototype without a product or release path does not qualify by itself.

designDefinitions.title: Design as visual coordination and evidence
designDefinitions.operationalTest: The visual artifact, board, screenshot, recording, diagram, or spatial surface primarily coordinates, explains, reviews, or verifies agent work rather than owning the implementation.
designDefinitions.boundary: A visual surface that directly owns the canonical graph or source belongs to native or code-visual authoring.

productForms.title: Standalone design-agent workspace
productForms.test: A dedicated product whose primary entry is AI-mediated design creation or refinement.

productForms.title: Design surface inside an agent platform
productForms.test: A named Design workspace or mode is one first-class surface within a broader coding or general-agent product.

productForms.title: General agent with visual tools
productForms.test: The product remains a general coding or execution agent; browser, preview, annotation, computer-use, or artifact viewers provide the visual path.

productForms.title: AI app or site builder
productForms.test: The primary product path turns intent into a hosted application or site and includes visual refinement and delivery.

productForms.title: Code-native visual editor or IDE
productForms.test: The product opens or creates executable source and makes its running projection a central visual authoring surface.

productForms.title: Runtime overlay or context bridge
productForms.test: An injected overlay, extension, compiler bridge, or preview picker captures targets and visual intent for another agent or editor.

productForms.title: Agent-controllable canvas or domain editor
productForms.test: A first-class visual artifact can be read or mutated by an external agent through tools, MCP, CLI, or a headless API.

productForms.title: Design-code bridge
productForms.test: The product's primary value is moving or grounding structured context between design and code rather than owning the full creation environment.

productForms.title: Established visual platform with AI
productForms.test: A pre-existing design, site, or application-authoring platform embeds agentic generation or control into its native artifact model.

productForms.title: Visual decision or verification workspace
productForms.test: The central surface arranges, compares, reviews, or captures alternatives and runtime evidence before another authority adopts the result.

productForms.title: Visual-editor infrastructure
productForms.test: The public project is primarily an embeddable editor kernel, schema, or interaction primitive rather than a complete end-user workspace.

architectureFamilies.title: Source-authority live projection
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Repository or workspace files are authoritative; a live visual projection maps deterministic edits or agent intent back to those files.

architectureFamilies.title: Runtime-intent relay
architectureFamilies.mechanism: A runtime overlay or browser bridge captures target context and desired change; another agent or editor owns durable source mutation.

architectureFamilies.title: Native graph authority
architectureFamilies.mechanism: A design, scene, site, page, or timeline graph is the canonical editable artifact and human or agent operations mutate its native objects.

architectureFamilies.title: External-agent canvas
architectureFamilies.mechanism: A separate visual artifact or canvas is exposed to third-party agents through MCP, skills, CLI, plugins, or a headless API.

architectureFamilies.title: Hosted generated-artifact workspace
architectureFamilies.mechanism: The provider owns generated code or artifact revisions and chat, visual, and code editing converge inside that hosted workspace.

architectureFamilies.title: Managed application-project graph
architectureFamilies.mechanism: A platform project spans UI, logic, data, backend, configuration, and release state; agent and visual edits mutate that managed graph.

architectureFamilies.title: Design-code materialization
architectureFamilies.mechanism: A design graph, capture, design system, or semantic join is compiled, exported, reconstructed, or grounded into a distinct code authority.

architectureFamilies.title: Filesystem agent with visual evidence
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Files and Git remain authoritative while canvases, screenshots, recordings, diagrams, or previews coordinate and verify the agent's work.

architectureFamilies.title: Candidate isolation and promotion
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Alternative designs, artifacts, or worktrees are isolated and compared; one candidate is explicitly selected, applied, or committed.
